target_customer: Marketers at web and e-commerce businesses without developer support
problem: Setting up web analytics and remarketing normally needs developers to add tracking code. Hublo let marketers click elements on a page to track them and build funnels without code.
business_model: B2B SaaS monthly subscription (basic plan about 49 euros per month in 2014)

founders.name: Cyril Gantzer
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says the idea came from his previous job at Fifty-five, an analytics consultancy for large French companies.

founders.name: Léo-Paul Goffic
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no background found.

founders.name: Etienne Le Scaon
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no background found in an opened source.

competitors.name: KISSmetrics
competitors.what: Customer analytics and funnels requiring code

technical_complexity.rationale: A visual point-and-click tagging layer over arbitrary customer sites with one script, funnels and e-commerce metrics, built by a very small team.

defensibility.rationale: The no-code angle was a feature that Mixpanel, Kissmetrics or Google Tag Manager could add; no data or network effects were described.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The acquirer and what happened to the product are not public in sources found.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in March 2014 framed analytics as locked behind developers, and the founder pitched the product as a Mailchimp for analytics based on his consulting experience at Fifty-five.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned as the analytics tool for the rest of us, friendly and non-technical per TechCrunch headline.

brand_strength.rationale: Only one press piece found. The name was later reused by an unrelated Paris healthcare staffing company, which confuses search results.

outcome_analysis: YC lists Hublo as acquired, but no source found names the acquirer, date or price, so the outcome cannot be explained. In 2014 it launched a no-code analytics product aimed at marketers, competing with Mixpanel and Kissmetrics, and no funding or traction figures are public.
notes: Company website field is empty and no live site was found, treated as dead. One search result claimed Etienne Le Scaon co-founded a company acquired by Criteo, dated 2013; unverified and not used. A later healthcare HR company named Hublo (Paris) is unrelated and its funding was excluded. Aggregator figures (Getlatka) are unreliable.
